anomalies.description: A sudden, bright flash of fire and dark smoke erupts from the ground in an open field, consistent with a detonation or explosion.
A large explosion occurs in an open field, producing a bright fireball followed by a rapidly expanding plume of black smoke and debris; the fire and smoke persist through the remainder of the clip.

A large, sudden explosion occurs with bright orange fireball and rapid expansion of dark smoke plume, consistent with a high-energy detonation.; Sustained post-detonation phase: massive black smoke column rises and spreads; residual fire visible at base through frames 10.5–12.0, then obscured by smoke and dust; no new blast events, but the event sequence originates from the initial explosion and continues as its direct consequence.

A large, sustained plume of thick black smoke rises rapidly from ground level, expanding and billowing upward and laterally across the frame, consistent with a major explosion or intense fireball event. The rapid onset at f0 (12.0s) and continued vigorous emission through f15 (19.5s) indicate an explosive origin rather than a slow-burning fire.

A large, rapidly expanding plume of dark smoke and debris erupts from the ground, consistent with a powerful explosion; the initial blast wave and rising column are visible across frames f0–f3.; Secondary or continuing explosive activity: turbulent smoke column continues to rise and expand, with visible ground disturbance and dust cloud propagation; possible secondary detonations or fuel fire contributing to sustained violent ejection (frames f3–f8).

A large, sustained plume of dark smoke and debris rises from the ground in an open field, expanding and churning over time—consistent with a powerful explosion or detonation event. The rapid initial expansion (f0–f3), followed by turbulent vertical and lateral dispersion (f4–f15), indicates a high-energy release rather than a fire or dust storm.

Post-blast phase: large smoke plume persists and drifts, with residual ground turbulence and dust still visible; no new detonation, but the event remains within the explosive aftermath window (frames f8–f15).
